items.title: Beginner
items.description: 1. Ask "does this make sense?" — the mistake couldn't be right in a real room, like a keyhole above a door handle. 2. Look before you tap: each miss costs an attempt. 3. Try the free hint in room 1 to see what a fix looks like.

items.title: Getting better
items.description: 4. Scan in a grid, one area at a time. 5. Check things that come in pairs or rows. 6. Think about how things work — doors, lights, furniture, clothes.

items.title: Lives
items.description: 7. Leaving a room costs a life, so keep looking while you have attempts. 8. Lives return every 30 minutes, even with the app closed. 9. Stuck? Share the room with a friend or watch a short video to see where to look. Out of taps? A video gives you two more.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers about the game, privacy, and purchases.

items.question: Is Tricky Rooms free?
items.answer: Yes. It's free to download and play, with optional in-app purchases: refill lives, buy a pack of 5 hints, or unlock Unlimited (unlimited lives and no banner or full-screen ads).

items.question: What age is it for?
items.answer: Everyone. Cartoon art, no violence, no chat and no user-generated content.

items.question: Does it work offline?
items.answer: Yes. All 30 rooms play offline. Ads, purchases and sharing need a connection.

items.question: Do I need an account?
items.answer: No. Your progress is saved on your device.

items.question: How many rooms are there?
items.answer: 30 rooms in 6 halls of 5 doors. Doors open in order.

items.question: How many taps do I get?
items.answer: 5 per room in the first hall, then 4, 3, and 2 in the last hall. A miss leaves a red scratch and costs one.

items.question: How do lives work?
items.answer: You have 5. Failing a room, trying again, or leaving a room after a tap costs one; backing out before your first tap is free. A new life arrives every 30 minutes, even with the app closed.

items.question: I'm stuck — any help?
items.answer: Share the room picture with friends from the fail screen, or watch a short video to see where to look. Out of taps? A video gives you two more.

items.question: Is this the old Tricky Rooms?
items.answer: It's a remaster of the 2014 original: the same rooms, art and music, rebuilt for today's phones and tablets. Progress from the old app doesn't carry over.

items.question: Will there be more rooms?
items.answer: Yes — more halls are planned and will arrive in free updates. Your progress carries straight on into them.

items.question: What ads are there?
items.answer: A banner on the win and fail screens, occasional full-screen ads between rooms (never in your first session or first five rooms), and optional videos you choose to watch for a life or a hint.

items.question: How do I restore Unlimited?
items.answer: Settings → Restore purchases, signed in with the same Apple ID or Google account.

items.question: How do I contact you?
items.answer: In the app: Settings → Send feedback. Or email zuki.apps.dev@gmail.com.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: Privacy Policy for Tricky Rooms — puzzle game. No accounts; progress stays on your device; how AdMob ads and Firebase diagnostics use data.
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how Zuki Apps handles information when you use Tricky Rooms and related pages at zukiapps.com/trickyrooms.

section1.title: 1. Who we are
section1.content: The data controller is Zuki Apps. Contact details are at the end of this Policy.
section1.content2: This Policy applies to the Tricky Rooms game and the legal pages we publish for it.

section2.title: 2. Information we collect
section2.content: Tricky Rooms has no accounts and we run no servers for it.
items: Game progress (rooms, lives, settings) stored only on your device and deleted when you uninstall
Advertising identifier, approximate location derived from your IP address, and ad interaction data collected by Google AdMob
Crash reports and anonymous usage statistics collected by Firebase Crashlytics and Analytics
Purchase records handled by Apple or Google — we never receive your payment details
Feedback and support messages you send us

section3.title: 3. How we use information
items: Show and measure ads (Google AdMob)
Fix crashes and improve the game
Validate in-app purchases
Reply to your messages
section3.content2: We do not sell your personal information.

section4.title: 4. Advertising and consent
section4.content: Where required, you are asked for consent before personalised ads are shown: Google's consent form in the EEA, UK, Switzerland and some US states, and Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt on iOS.
section4.content2: You can change ad consent in the app's settings and limit ad tracking in your device settings (iOS: Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking; Android: Settings → Google → Ads).

section5.title: 5. Storage and security
section5.content: Game progress never leaves your device. Data sent by the SDKs is encrypted in transit.
section5.content2: Ad, analytics and purchase partners retain data under their own policies.

section6.title: 6. Third-party services
section6.content: Google AdMob and Firebase process data under Google's privacy policy. In-app purchases are processed by Apple App Store or Google Play Billing under their policies.
section6.content2: Sharing a room picture uses your device's share sheet; we do not see what you share or with whom.

section7.title: 7. Your rights and children
section7.content: Depending on your region you may have rights to access or delete data. Delete all game data by uninstalling, or email zuki.apps.dev@gmail.com and we will help.
section7.content2: Tricky Rooms is not directed at children under 13.

section8.title: 8. Changes
section8.content: We may update this Policy from time to time. We will post the revised version with a new Last updated date.
